Container.Name: Purser
Container.Overview:
Purser is an open-source model supply-chain control plane: it scans ML model artifacts for malicious code and data-exfiltration indicators, checks provenance/signatures, and renders one policy verdict (PASS / WARN / FAIL / BLOCKED).
It never loads or executes a model — all analysis is byte- and opcode-level — and format is detected by magic bytes rather than filename, so a payload renamed to look benign is still caught. Runs fully offline.
Point the Model store path at your share (or at ~/.ollama/models to check models pulled by Ollama; extensionless sha256- blobs are recognised as GGUF automatically). The WebUI link performs a health check; use the CLI or the REST API to run scans.
Note: a PASS means "clear of known malicious content", not "certified safe". Purser does not detect trained/behavioural backdoors.

Config.Name: WebUI Port
Config.Description: Port for the REST API and /healthz.

Config.Name: Model store
Config.Description: Your model share, mounted READ-ONLY. Purser never writes to it.

Config.Name: API key
Config.Description: Require this key on /v1 endpoints (Bearer or X-API-Key). STRONGLY recommended if the port is reachable beyond your LAN — with no key set, /v1 is open by design for trusted networks.

Config.Name: Policy file
Config.Description: Policy path inside the container. The image ships /policies/default.yaml. Mount your own policy directory to use strict.yaml or signed-only.yaml.

Config.Name: Scan root
Config.Description: Paths passed to the scan API must resolve under this root.

Config.Name: Max scan size (MB)
Config.Description: Skip files larger than this. Raise for large GGUF or multi-GB checkpoints.

Config.Name: Max concurrent scans
Config.Description: Concurrency cap. Keep low on a NAS so scanning does not starve other containers.

Config.Name: Custom policies
Config.Description: Optional: a directory of policy YAML files, mounted read-only. Leave unset to use the policy baked into the image.
